title: Apple Inc. (AAPL) Shares Bought by First Hawaiian Bank
text:
Posted by ABMN Staff on Jan 13th, 2019 // No Comments
First Hawaiian Bank raised its holdings in shares of Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 720.0% in the 3rd quarter, according to its most recent filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission. The institutional investor owned 82,101 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after acquiring an additional 72,089 shares during the quarter. Apple makes up approximately 1.0% of First Hawaiian Bank’s holdings, making the stock its 12th biggest position. First Hawaiian Bank’s holdings in Apple were worth $18,534,000 at the end of the most recent quarter.
Several other institutional investors and hedge funds have also modified their holdings of the company. Nikko Asset Management Americas Inc. grew its stake in shares of Apple by 4.1% during the 3rd quarter. Nikko Asset Management Americas Inc. now owns 649,566 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $148,731,000 after acquiring an additional 25,873 shares in the last quarter. Gardiner Nancy B grew its stake in shares of Apple by 49.5% in the third quarter. Gardiner Nancy B now owns 11,625 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $2,624,000 after buying an additional 3,850 shares in the last quarter. Sheets Smith Wealth Management grew its stake in shares of Apple by 20.7% in the third quarter. Sheets Smith Wealth Management now owns 50,986 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $11,510,000 after buying an additional 8,746 shares in the last quarter. Cookson Peirce & Co. Inc. grew its stake in shares of Apple by 2.1% in the third quarter. Cookson Peirce & Co. Inc. now owns 172,154 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $38,862,000 after buying an additional 3,569 shares in the last quarter. Finally, Kessler Investment Group LLC grew its stake in shares of Apple by 24.9% in the third quarter. Kessler Investment Group LLC now owns 29,416 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock valued at $6,640,000 after buying an additional 5,864 shares in the last quarter. 57.06% of the stock is owned by institutional investors. AAPL stock opened at $152.29 on Friday. The stock has a market capitalization of $753.54 billion, a P/E ratio of 12.79, a P/E/G ratio of 1.45 and a beta of 1.23. Apple Inc. has a 52 week low of $142.00 and a 52 week high of $233.47. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.87, a current ratio of 1.12 and a quick ratio of 1.09.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last posted its quarterly earnings results on Thursday, November 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.91 EPS for the quarter, beating the Zacks’ consensus estimate of $2.78 by $0.13. The business had revenue of $62.90 billion during the quarter, compared to the consensus estimate of $61.55 billion. Apple had a return on equity of 48.68% and a net margin of 22.41%. Apple’s revenue for the quarter was up 19.6% compared to the same quarter last year. During the same quarter in the previous year, the firm earned $2.07 earnings per share. On average, sell-side analysts predict that Apple Inc. will post 12.1 earnings per share for the current fiscal year.
A number of research firms have commented on AAPL. Maxim Group reduced their price objective on shares of Apple from $212.00 to $160.00 and set a “hold” rating for the company in a research report on Thursday, January 3rd. They noted that the move was a valuation call. Daiwa Capital Markets set a $200.00 price objective on shares of Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research report on Friday, January 4th. Royal Bank of Canada set a $185.00 price objective on shares of Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a research report on Thursday, January 3rd. Wedbush reaffirmed an “outperform” rating and set a $200.00 price objective (down from $275.00) on shares of Apple in a research report on Thursday, January 3rd. Finally, Robert W. Baird reduced their price objective on shares of Apple from $230.00 to $185.00 and set an “outperform” rating for the company in a research report on Thursday, January 3rd. Three research analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, twenty-six have assigned a hold rating and twenty-two have given a buy rating to the company. Apple has a consensus rating of “Hold” and a consensus target price of $195.19.
In other Apple news, insider Chris Kondo sold 3,408 shares of the business’s stock in a transaction dated Monday, November 19th. The stock was sold at an average price of $190.00, for a total transaction of $647,520.00. Following the completion of the transaction, the insider now owns 8,940 shares of the company’s stock, valued at $1,698,600. About Apple
Apple Inc designs, manufactures, and markets mobile communication and media devices, and personal computers. It also sells various related software, services, accessories, and third-party digital content and applications. The company offers iPhone, a line of smartphones; iPad, a line of multi-purpose tablets; and Mac, a line of desktop and portable personal computers, as well as iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS operating systems.
